correctness.rationale: Switching the first row of a real \(4\times4\) signature matrix positive leaves three signs. The all-positive and all-negative patterns give the tight/impossible spectral cases, while all six mixed patterns have characteristic polynomial \((t^2-1)(t^2-5)\), form one switching-permutation class, and force coherence \(1/\sqrt5\). For a representative Gram matrix \(G\), the displayed kernel vector spans \(\ker G\), and the canonical dual Gram is \(K=G^\dagger\), giving the stated raw off-diagonal moduli and two norm classes. Every symmetric generalized inverse satisfying \(GHG=G\) has form \(H=K+za^{\mathsf T}+az^{\mathsf T}\). Imposing one common off-diagonal modulus leaves \(32\) relative sign patterns. An independent exact symbolic reconstruction over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)\) confirmed that \(20\) systems are inconsistent and all \(12\) consistent systems have nonzero determinant, so none can be a Gram matrix of four vectors in \(\mathbb R^3\). This independently reproduces the load-bearing package computation.
residual_risks: The result is specific to real four-vector frames in dimension three.

originality.rationale: The literature comparison materially narrows the novelty claim. Datta's 2021 chapter already exhibits the same non-tight real \((4,3)\) equiangular switching class with coherence \(1/\sqrt5\) and computes a canonical dual with two normalized angles; the 2020 Christensen--Datta--Kim article develops canonical-dual few-angle criteria. Those prior results therefore cover the frame classification and substantial canonical-dual geometry. However, neither complete inspected source proves that no arbitrary dual can have one common off-diagonal Gram modulus. The audited generalized-inverse classification and complete \(32\)-sign-pattern rank obstruction answer the broader all-duals existence question posed by this literature. Resultary returned no prior all-duals obstruction.
